chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together, from Al-Hajjal, from Thalabah, from Hafs Al-Awr, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The large jar in which wine has been kept, then it is dried out, and vinegar is made in it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Is a wine jar pure after the wine dries up and vinegar is made in it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that a *dann* (a large earthenware jar) previously holding wine becomes pure (*tahir*) once the wine residue dries, allowing vinegar to be made or stored within it. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the drying of wine residue removes its impurity (*najasa*), distinguishing it from cases where the liquid remains or is merely rinsed, thereby facilitating the transformation of the vessel's status for culinary use.
